name: Omelette Soufflée (Baked)
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: Juice of a lemon and half the peel, grated
ingredients.originalText: Juice of a lemon and half the peel, grated

instructions.text: Beat yolks and whites separately and very well
Add to the yolks by degrees the powdered sugar, and beat until it ceases to froth, and is thick and smooth
The whites should be stiff enough to cut with a knife
Stir together lightly with the seasoning
Bake in a quick oven five or six minutes
The dish should be warmed when it is buttered, not to chill the eggs
Send around with a spoon, and let each one help himself before it can fall

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Beat yolks and whites separately and very well
2. Add to the yolks by degrees the powdered sugar, and beat until it ceases to froth, and is thick and smooth
3. The whites should be stiff enough to cut with a knife
4. Stir together lightly with the seasoning
5. Pour into a well-buttered dish
6. Bake in a quick oven five or six minutes
7. The dish should be warmed when it is buttered, not to chill the eggs
8. Send around with a spoon, and let each one help himself before it can fall
originalIngredients: Juice of a lemon and half the peel, grated
